title: One crown, one parliament?
hook: Does sharing a monarch tell you how lawmaking is organised?

knows: A monarch and a parliament name different kinds of institution; two dated documentary fields can be compared.
doesNotKnow: Sharing a monarch need not establish a shared parliament; named institutional relations need their own documentary evidence.

misconception: Sharing a monarch establishes a shared parliament.
objective: Distinguish a shared monarch from a shared parliament using the separately sourced 1603 and 1707 institutional relations.

recall.question: Two kingdoms share a monarch. What evidence would establish a shared lawmaking institution?
recall.why: A shared monarch alone does not establish a shared parliament; check evidence about the parliamentary institution.

care: Show the named parliamentary institutions; do not make their records stand for popular consent or uniform law.
